note: All dates are NASA figures; future dates are NASA targets and shift. Updated by scripts/update-artemis.js (flags changes; never invents data).

missions.name: Artemis I
missions.synopsis: NASA's first flight test of SLS, Orion and ground systems: an uncrewed 25-day trip beyond the Moon, launched Nov. 16 and splashed down Dec. 11, 2022.
missions.status: Flown. Uncrewed flight test, Nov. 16 to Dec. 11, 2022.
missions.objective: Test the rocket, spacecraft and ground systems without a crew.

missions.name: Artemis II
missions.status: Flown. Four astronauts flew around the Moon, reached 252,756 miles from Earth on April 6, 2026, and splashed down off San Diego after a nearly 10-day, 695,081-mile journey.
missions.objective: Prove Orion and SLS with a crew aboard.

milestones.label: Launch on SLS and Orion from Kennedy Space Center

sources.label: NASA, Artemis II crew back on Earth

missions.synopsis: Four astronauts flew around the Moon in April 2026 and reached 252,756 miles from Earth, farther than any humans before.

missions.name: Artemis III
missions.status: A crewed test flight in low Earth orbit, planned for 14 days: Orion will dock first with a test version of Blue Origin's Blue Moon lander, then with a test version of SpaceX's Starship, and test critical systems before any landing. No launch date set yet, so no countdown.
missions.objective: Demonstrate Critical Systems for Lunar Landing
missions.hardware: SLS, Orion, and test versions of both human landing systems: Blue Origin Blue Moon Mark 2 and SpaceX Starship (company-built, NASA contracts).

milestones.label: NASA makes Artemis III an Earth-orbit test; first landing moves to Artemis IV
Crew named: Bresnik, Parmitano (ESA), Douglas, Rubio
NASA details the plan: a 14-day mission docking with Blue Moon and Starship test versions

missions.synopsis: A crewed test in low Earth orbit: Orion practices docking with test versions of both commercial lunar landers before any landing.

missions.name: Artemis IV
missions.status: Humanity's return to the lunar surface: two of four crew will descend near the Moon's South Pole and spend about a week there. Crew not yet announced.
missions.objective: Land two astronauts near the lunar South Pole for about a week of science.
missions.hardware: SLS (standardized configuration from Artemis IV), Orion docking with a commercial human landing system in lunar orbit. Gateway is not listed in NASA's February 2026 plan update.

milestones.label: NASA names Artemis IV the first crewed landing, targeted for 2028

sources.label: NASA, Return to the lunar surface plan (Mar 2026)

missions.synopsis: Humanity's return to the lunar surface: two astronauts spend about a week near the Moon's South Pole.

missions.name: Artemis V
missions.synopsis: A second astronaut landing in NASA's February 2026 plan.
missions.status: NASA's February 2026 plan lists Artemis V as an additional astronaut landing, targeting late 2028. No mission page or crew yet.
missions.objective: An additional astronaut landing on the Moon.
missions.hardware: SLS, Orion and a commercial human landing system (per NASA's plan).

milestones.label: Added to NASA's updated Artemis plan

sources.label: NASA, Return to the lunar surface plan (Mar 2026)
